name: Bog Hag

alignment.name: Evil
alignment.description:
Evil creatures don’t necessarily go out of their way to hurt people, but they’re perfectly willing to take advantage of the weakness of others to acquire what they want.
	Evil creatures use rules and order to maximize personal gain. They don’t care whether laws hurt other people. They support institutional structures that give them power, even if that power comes at the expense of others’ freedom. Slavery and rigid caste structures are not only acceptable but desirable to evil creatures, as long as they are in a position to benefit from them.

description: This is the size of a typical human and serves as a standard in the game. This category has no special rules.

traits.name: Unwholesome Presence
traits.details: When an enemy within the aura spends a healing surge to regain hit points, that enemy regains only half the normal hit points.

traits.name: Aquatic
traits.details: The hag can breathe underwater. In aquatic combat, it gains a +2 bonus to attack rolls against nonaquatic creatures.

traits.name: Evasive Charge
traits.details: The hag can take a single free action to shift up to 2 squares immediately after charging.

auras.name: Unwholesome Presence
auras.details: When an enemy within the aura spends a healing surge to regain hit points, that enemy regains only half the normal hit points.

effect.description: The hag can shift up to 2 squares.
The hag uses claw twice against the same target. If both attacks hit, the target takes 5 extra damage.

The hag alters its physical form to appear as a young female elf, half-elf, eladrin, or human until it uses change shape again or until it drops to 0 hit points. To assume a specific individual’s form, the hag must have seen that individual. Other creatures can make a DC 31 Insight check to discern that the form is a disguise.
